### Data types

* [`Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName`](#Dnsmasq--DhcpOptionName): A DHCP option: a number, a bare option name, or a name prefixed with `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:`.
* [`Dnsmasq::Hwaddr`](#Dnsmasq--Hwaddr): A hardware address for `dhcp-host`, optionally prefixed with an ARP type and allowing `*` wildcards.
* [`Dnsmasq::LeaseTime`](#Dnsmasq--LeaseTime): A DHCP lease time: seconds, a number with an `m`, `h`, `d` or `w` suffix, or `infinite`.
* [`Dnsmasq::Name`](#Dnsmasq--Name): A DNS or DHCP name as written in a dnsmasq option: no commas, slashes or whitespace.
* [`Dnsmasq::OptionName`](#Dnsmasq--OptionName): A dnsmasq long option name, without leading dashes.
* [`Dnsmasq::OptionValue`](#Dnsmasq--OptionValue): A value in the `dnsmasq::options` hash.
* [`Dnsmasq::Order`](#Dnsmasq--Order): The position of a line within its per-type file. Lines sort numerically, then by title.
* [`Dnsmasq::Tag`](#Dnsmasq--Tag): A dnsmasq tag name, as used with `set:`.
* [`Dnsmasq::TagMatch`](#Dnsmasq--TagMatch): A dnsmasq tag to match with `tag:`. A leading `!` negates the match.
* [`Dnsmasq::TagMatches`](#Dnsmasq--TagMatches): One or more tags to match with `tag:`.

## Classes

### <a name="dnsmasq"></a>`dnsmasq`

`/etc/dnsmasq.conf` only loads `config_dir`. Free-form options are written to
`10-options.conf`; each typed resource is written to one file per type, such as
`50-host-record.conf`. Every hash parameter below creates resources of the named
defined type, keyed by title, and is deep-merged across the Hiera hierarchy.

#### Examples

##### Hiera

```puppet
dnsmasq::options:
  domain: example.com
  expand-hosts: true
  dhcp-authoritative: true
dnsmasq::host_records:
  router.example.com:
    ip: 192.0.2.1
dnsmasq::dhcp_ranges:
  home:
    start: 192.0.2.50
    end: 192.0.2.99
    lease_time: 2d
```

## Defined types

### <a name="dnsmasq--address"></a>`dnsmasq::address`

Without `ip`, the domains are local-only and answer NXDOMAIN for unknown names.

#### Examples

##### Return NXDOMAIN for unknown names in example.com instead of forwarding

```puppet
dnsmasq::address { 'example.com': }
```

##### Return a fixed address for a domain and all its subdomains

```puppet
dnsmasq::address { 'ads.example.net': ip => '0.0.0.0' }
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `dnsmasq::address` defined type:

* [`domains`](#-dnsmasq--address--domains)
* [`ip`](#-dnsmasq--address--ip)
* [`order`](#-dnsmasq--address--order)

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--address--domains"></a>`domains`

Data type: `Variant[Dnsmasq::Name, Array[Dnsmasq::Name, 1]]`

The domains. `#` matches every domain.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--address--ip"></a>`ip`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[Stdlib::IP::Address::Nosubnet, Enum['#']]]`

The address to answer with, or `#` for the null address in both families.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--address--order"></a>`order`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Order`

The position within `50-address.conf`.

Default value: `50`

### <a name="dnsmasq--caa_record"></a>`dnsmasq::caa_record`

A CAA record (`caa-record`).

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
dnsmasq::caa_record { 'example.com': property => 'issue', value => 'letsencrypt.org' }
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `dnsmasq::caa_record` defined type:

* [`property`](#-dnsmasq--caa_record--property)
* [`value`](#-dnsmasq--caa_record--value)
* [`flags`](#-dnsmasq--caa_record--flags)
* [`record_name`](#-dnsmasq--caa_record--record_name)
* [`order`](#-dnsmasq--caa_record--order)

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--caa_record--property"></a>`property`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9]+\z/]`

The property tag, e.g. `issue`, `issuewild` or `iodef`.

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--caa_record--value"></a>`value`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^,]+\z/]`

The property value. Must not contain commas.

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--caa_record--flags"></a>`flags`

Data type: `Integer[0, 255]`

The CAA flags; 128 marks the property critical.

Default value: `0`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--caa_record--record_name"></a>`record_name`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Name`

The name the record is for.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--caa_record--order"></a>`order`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Order`

The position within `50-caa-record.conf`.

Default value: `50`

### <a name="dnsmasq--dhcp_match"></a>`dnsmasq::dhcp_match`

Set a tag when a client sends a DHCP option (`dhcp-match`).

#### Examples

##### Tag iPXE clients that support HTTP

```puppet
dnsmasq::dhcp_match { 'ipxe-http': option => 175, value => 19 }
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `dnsmasq::dhcp_match` defined type:

* [`option`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--option)
* [`value`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--value)

* [`order`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--order)

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--option"></a>`option`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName`

The option: a number, a bare name such as `client-arch` (written as `option:client-arch`),
or a name with an `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:` prefix.

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--value"></a>`value`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String[1], Integer]]`

Only match when the option has this value.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--set"></a>`set`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Tag`

The tag to set.

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_match--order"></a>`order`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Order`

The position within `50-dhcp-match.conf`.

Default value: `50`

### <a name="dnsmasq--dhcp_option"></a>`dnsmasq::dhcp_option`

A DHCP option sent to clients (`dhcp-option` or `dhcp-option-force`).

#### Examples

##### Per-network router, selected by the tag set on a dhcp_range

```puppet
dnsmasq::dhcp_option { 'home router': option => 'router', value => '192.0.2.1', tags => 'home' }
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `dnsmasq::dhcp_option` defined type:

* [`option`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--option)

* [`tags`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--tags)

* [`vendor`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--vendor)

* [`order`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--order)

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--option"></a>`option`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName`

The option: a number, a bare name such as `router` (written as `option:router`),
or a name with an `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:` prefix.

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--value"></a>`value`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Integer, Array[Variant[String, Integer]]]]`

The option value. An array is joined with commas.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--tags"></a>`tags`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::TagMatches`

Only send to clients with these tags.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--encap"></a>`encap`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0, 255]]`

Encapsulate within this option number.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--vi_encap"></a>`vi_encap`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

Encapsulate as vendor-identifying vendor-specific information for this enterprise number.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--vendor"></a>`vendor`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Send as vendor-specific information to clients with this vendor class. An empty string matches any.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--force"></a>`force`

Data type: `Boolean`

Send the option even when the client does not request it.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_option--order"></a>`order`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Order`

The position within `50-dhcp-option.conf`.

Default value: `50`

### <a name="dnsmasq--dhcp_range"></a>`dnsmasq::dhcp_range`

A DHCP address range (`dhcp-range`), IPv4 or IPv6 according to `start`.

#### Examples

##### IPv4 range tagged for per-network options

```puppet
dnsmasq::dhcp_range { 'home':
  start      => '192.0.2.50',
  end        => '192.0.2.99',
  netmask    => '255.255.255.0',
  lease_time => '2d',
  set        => 'home',
}
```

##### IPv6 SLAAC with names, addresses taken from an interface

```puppet
dnsmasq::dhcp_range { 'home6':
  start       => '::',
  constructor => 'eth0',
  modes       => ['ra-names'],
  prefix_length => 64,
  lease_time  => '24h',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `dnsmasq::dhcp_range` defined type:

* [`start`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--start)
* [`end`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--end)
* [`constructor`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--constructor)
* [`modes`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--modes)
* [`netmask`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--netmask)
* [`broadcast`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--broadcast)
* [`prefix_length`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--prefix_length)
* [`lease_time`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--lease_time)
* [`tags`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--tags)
* [`set`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--set)
* [`order`](#-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--order)

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--start"></a>`start`

Data type: `Stdlib::IP::Address::Nosubnet`

The first address, or the network address with `modes` such as `static` or `proxy`.

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--end"></a>`end`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::Nosubnet]`

The last address.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--constructor"></a>`constructor`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

IPv6 only: build the range from this interface's prefix. Replaces `end`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--modes"></a>`modes`

Data type: `Array[Pattern[/\A[a-z-]+\z/]]`

Mode keywords such as `static`, `proxy`, `ra-only`, `ra-names`, `ra-stateless`, `slaac`.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--netmask"></a>`netmask`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet]`

IPv4 only: the netmask, needed when the range is not on a local interface.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--broadcast"></a>`broadcast`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet]`

IPv4 only: the broadcast address. Requires `netmask`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--prefix_length"></a>`prefix_length`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1, 128]]`

IPv6 only: the prefix length.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--lease_time"></a>`lease_time`

Data type: `Optional[Dnsmasq::LeaseTime]`

The lease time.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--tags"></a>`tags`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::TagMatches`

Only use this range for clients with these tags.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--set"></a>`set`

Data type: `Optional[Dnsmasq::Tag]`

Set this tag on clients served from this range.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-dnsmasq--dhcp_range--order"></a>`order`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::Order`

The position within `50-dhcp-range.conf`.

Default value: `50`

## Functions

### <a name="dnsmasq--dhcp_option_name"></a>`dnsmasq::dhcp_option_name`

Type: Puppet Language

Numbers and names already carrying an `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:` prefix
are returned unchanged; a bare name such as `router` becomes `option:router`.

#### `dnsmasq::dhcp_option_name(Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName $option)`

Numbers and names already carrying an `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:` prefix
are returned unchanged; a bare name such as `router` becomes `option:router`.

Returns: `String` The option as dnsmasq expects it.

##### `option`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName`

The option number or name.

### <a name="dnsmasq--line"></a>`dnsmasq::line`

Type: Puppet Language

Fields are flattened and joined with commas. Trailing `undef` fields are dropped;
`undef` fields followed by a defined field render as empty, which dnsmasq treats
as "not given" for positional arguments such as the server name in `dhcp-boot`.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
dnsmasq::line('dhcp-boot', ['menu.ipxe', undef, '192.0.2.1']) # => "dhcp-boot=menu.ipxe,,192.0.2.1\n"
```

#### `dnsmasq::line(Dnsmasq::OptionName $option, Array $fields = [])`

Fields are flattened and joined with commas. Trailing `undef` fields are dropped;
`undef` fields followed by a defined field render as empty, which dnsmasq treats
as "not given" for positional arguments such as the server name in `dhcp-boot`.

Returns: `String` The option line, terminated by a newline.

##### Examples

######

```puppet
dnsmasq::line('dhcp-boot', ['menu.ipxe', undef, '192.0.2.1']) # => "dhcp-boot=menu.ipxe,,192.0.2.1\n"
```

##### `option`

Data type: `Dnsmasq::OptionName`

The dnsmasq long option name, without leading dashes.

##### `fields`

Data type: `Array`

The comma-separated values for the option.

### <a name="dnsmasq--quote"></a>`dnsmasq::quote`

Type: Puppet Language

Quote a string for a dnsmasq configuration file so that it may contain commas.

#### `dnsmasq::quote(String $value)`

The dnsmasq::quote function.

Returns: `String` The value in double quotes, with `\` and `"` escaped.

##### `value`

Data type: `String`

The string to quote.

### <a name="dnsmasq--render_options"></a>`dnsmasq::render_options`

Type: Puppet Language

Render the `dnsmasq::options` hash as configuration lines, in hash order.

#### `dnsmasq::render_options(Hash[Dnsmasq::OptionName, Dnsmasq::OptionValue] $options)`

The dnsmasq::render_options function.

Returns: `String` The rendered lines.

##### `options`

Data type: `Hash[Dnsmasq::OptionName, Dnsmasq::OptionValue]`

Option names mapped to values. `true` writes a bare flag, `false` omits the
option, and an array writes the option once per element.

### <a name="dnsmasq--tags"></a>`dnsmasq::tags`

Type: Puppet Language

Render the `tag:` and `set:` fields that lead many DHCP options.

#### `dnsmasq::tags(Variant[Dnsmasq::TagMatches, Undef] $match = [], Variant[Dnsmasq::Tag, Array[Dnsmasq::Tag], Undef] $set = [])`

The dnsmasq::tags function.

Returns: `Array[String]` The fields, match tags first.

##### `match`

Data type: `Variant[Dnsmasq::TagMatches, Undef]`

Tags to match, rendered as `tag:<name>`.

##### `set`

Data type: `Variant[Dnsmasq::Tag, Array[Dnsmasq::Tag], Undef]`

Tags to set, rendered as `set:<name>`.

## Data types

### <a name="Dnsmasq--DhcpOptionName"></a>`Dnsmasq::DhcpOptionName`

A DHCP option: a number, a bare option name, or a name prefixed with `option:`, `option6:` or `vi-encap:`.

Alias of `Variant[Integer[0, 65535], Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:-]*\z/]]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--Hwaddr"></a>`Dnsmasq::Hwaddr`

A hardware address for `dhcp-host`, optionally prefixed with an ARP type and allowing `*` wildcards.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A([0-9]+-)?[0-9A-Fa-f*]{1,2}([:-][0-9A-Fa-f*]{1,2}){5,19}\z/]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--LeaseTime"></a>`Dnsmasq::LeaseTime`

A DHCP lease time: seconds, a number with an `m`, `h`, `d` or `w` suffix, or `infinite`.

Alias of `Variant[Integer[120], Pattern[/\A[0-9]+[smhdw]?\z/], Enum['infinite']]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--Name"></a>`Dnsmasq::Name`

A DNS or DHCP name as written in a dnsmasq option: no commas, slashes or whitespace.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[^\s,\/]+\z/]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--OptionName"></a>`Dnsmasq::OptionName`

A dnsmasq long option name, without leading dashes.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\z/]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--OptionValue"></a>`Dnsmasq::OptionValue`

`true` writes the bare option, `false` omits it, an array writes the option once per element.

Alias of `Variant[Boolean, String, Integer, Array[Variant[String, Integer]]]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--Order"></a>`Dnsmasq::Order`

The position of a line within its per-type file. Lines sort numerically, then by title.

Alias of `Integer[1, 999]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--Tag"></a>`Dnsmasq::Tag`

A dnsmasq tag name, as used with `set:`.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[^\s,:!]+\z/]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--TagMatch"></a>`Dnsmasq::TagMatch`

A dnsmasq tag to match with `tag:`. A leading `!` negates the match.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A!?[^\s,:!]+\z/]`

### <a name="Dnsmasq--TagMatches"></a>`Dnsmasq::TagMatches`

One or more tags to match with `tag:`.

Alias of `Variant[Dnsmasq::TagMatch, Array[Dnsmasq::TagMatch]]`
